plan: With a private value of $9, I want to maximize potential profit. In Stage 2's descending clock mechanism, I'll aim to claim the item just above my value. Since my value is $9, I'll bid strategically to win if the clock drops to near my value. A bid around $9.50 seems optimal - high enough to potentially win, but not so high that I lose money if I acquire the item. This balances winning probability with profit margin.

In a single-round sealed bid auction with a descending clock, my optimal strategy is to bid close to, but slightly below my private value of $9. If I bid too high, I risk paying more than my value. If I bid too low, I might lose the item. Given the uncertainty of other bidders' values, I'll aim to bid around $8, which gives me a small buffer while still having a good chance of winning.

In this single-round sealed bid auction, my goal is to maximize profit. With a private value of $34, I want to bid strategically. Since the descending clock starts at $49 and I'll win if my sealed bid is the highest, I'll aim to bid just below my value. A bid around $33-$34 balances claiming the item if my bid is competitive while preserving potential profit margin.
